title: Tools for Shopify merchants, from a small Shopify merchant
subtitle: Expertise run for a home-goods Shopify store owner: 17 apps across 9 categories scouted from 1- to 3-star App Store reviews, then a deep dive on post-Stocky inventory purchasing.

founder.skills: simple web apps with AI help; runs a ~$8k/mo home-goods Shopify store

verdict.summary: The pain is real: small POS retailers lost Stocky on Aug 31, 2026, and they say Shopify's native POs take triple the time. But don't build another Stocky replacement app. A free, 4.9-rated one (Stockroom) and more than ten cheap apps already cover it, and these shops resist new monthly fees. The pivot is to change the channel and price: sell a one-time $199 setup service on top of the free tools, and run the 7-day test before building anything. Read-only Stocky access ends Nov 29, so test now.

opportunities.name: Stocky replacement app for small POS retailers
opportunities.one_liner: POs, receiving, labels and stock counts for brick-and-mortar Shopify shops after Stocky's shutdown.
opportunities.why: Strongest pain in the scout: Stocky is rated 3.0 with 28% one-star reviews and was shut down, merchants call native POs brutally inadequate, and some are leaving Shopify POS. But Stockroom is free and unlimited, rated 4.9, and more than ten other apps pitch in the same threads at $0 to $20. Shops cap spend at $100/mo and resent paying for what was free.

opportunities.name: Wholesale ordering for small makers
opportunities.one_liner: Reliable wholesale pricing and net terms for small brands selling to boutiques.
opportunities.why: Merchants lose wholesale orders when pricing isn't applied or net terms fail, and they pay $35 to $149/mo for apps. But Shopify B2B now runs on Basic and up, and pricing logic touches checkout and themes. Not deep-dived; needs its own run.

opportunities.name: Subscriptions for small merchants
opportunities.one_liner: Subscribe-and-save without percentage fees for brands with a few hundred subscribers.
opportunities.why: Recharge users complain about no small tier, fees above 10% of recurring revenue, and lock-in. But Seal is free up to 50 subscriptions with 0% fees, Shopify Subscriptions is free, and recurring billing is high-stakes for a 10-hour-a-week builder.

gap.statement: Small brick-and-mortar Shopify shops forced off Stocky can't get purchasing, receiving and labels running again without days of re-entering vendor and supplier data, because every replacement is self-serve software and Shopify's tools can't carry suppliers across.

pains.theme: Shopify took away the tool we run the shop on
pains.summary: Stocky was neglected, stripped of features, then shut down; some shops are leaving Shopify POS.

pains.theme: The native PO tool takes triple the time
pains.summary: Native POs are slow for many-SKU orders and have no fill-shelves reordering.
Suppliers can't be exported from Stocky, and native POs force vendors to be re-created as suppliers.

pains.theme: Won't pay $100+/mo for what used to be free
pains.summary: Small shops resist new fees; forecasting suites price for bigger stores and raise prices at renewal.

pains.theme: Nobody can help me set it up
pains.summary: Support can't fix it, setup eats whole days, and real onboarding costs thousands.

pains.theme: Labels and stock counts don't work
pains.summary: Receiving labels and barcode counts break, so shops pay for extra apps.
Sync breaks, forecasts miss seasonality, data has bugs.

critic.rebuttal: Native POs are still called brutally inadequate (e7, e8), and a setup service works on whichever tool Shopify pushes.

critic.rebuttal: They move files; merchants are still asking months later how to map vendors, print labels and train staff (e15, e16, e34).

validation.experiment: Post one help thread, answer 8 to 10 open questions in the Stocky threads, and message 10 named Stocky reviewers; point all of it at the landing page with a $99 founding offer.
validation.pass_bar: 3 shops pay (or put down a $50 deposit), or 10 booked calls from different shops

Day 2: post the export checklist thread
Day 5: answer 4 more threads, follow up on replies

Day 7: count payments, calls and objections; decide
